summary: Adds an admin route that deletes one user by id and a route that purges a list of users.

findings.title: User delete route lacks the admin check
findings.problem: The DELETE /users/:id route does not use requireAdmin, while its sibling routes do. The admin router has no router-level guard, and server.js mounts it without one.
findings.consequence: Any caller who can reach the server can delete any user by id. This is broken authorization on a destructive action.
findings.fix: Add requireAdmin as middleware on the delete route, matching the other admin routes.

findings.title: Purge drops removeUser promises
findings.problem: The purge handler passes an async callback to forEach, so nothing awaits or catches the removeUser promises. The handler replies with ids.length before any removal finishes.
findings.consequence: removeUser throws for an unknown id, and that rejection goes unhandled, which crashes the Node process by default. The client also gets a removed count that ignores failures.
findings.fix: Await Promise.allSettled over ids.map(db.removeUser), then report the count of fulfilled results.
findings.suggested_change:
const results = await Promise.allSettled(ids.map((id) => db.removeUser(id)));
  res.json({ removed: results.filter((r) => r.status === "fulfilled").length });

findings.title: New admin routes have no tests
findings.problem: The change adds a delete route and a purge route. No test in the repository exercises either route.
findings.consequence: Nothing catches regressions in authorization or in error handling on these destructive routes.
findings.fix: Add tests that cover the admin check, the 400 path, and purge with an unknown id.
